group.description: The detail work that separates a correct surface from a beautiful one. Declared in full so the intended standard is visible and plannable; deliberately capped below machine tier because most of it is judgment. Entries are promoted individually as checkers become possible.

capabilities.title: Icons share one optical weight
capabilities.description: Icons rendered together share stroke width, corner treatment, and optical size, so a row of controls reads as one family rather than as assets from different sets.
capabilities.rationale: Partly deterministic once an icon registry normalizes geometry — stroke width and box size become comparable numbers. Optical size, which is what the eye actually judges, is not.

capabilities.title: Headings and labels break well
capabilities.description: Multi-line headings and labels break into balanced lines with no single orphaned word, and truncation happens at a meaningful boundary rather than mid-token.
capabilities.rationale: Orphan detection is mechanical. Whether a given break reads well is not, and it varies by locale — German compounds and Japanese line breaking have different notions of a good break.

capabilities.title: The cursor tells the truth
capabilities.description: Cursor treatment matches what an element actually does: pointer for activation, text for selectable content, grab for draggable objects, not-allowed for disabled, and default for everything inert.
capabilities.rationale: The most deterministic entry in this group — cursor is a computed style and the correct value follows from the element's role and disabled state. Likely the first craft capability to be promoted to machine tier.

capabilities.title: Empty states teach rather than apologize
capabilities.description: An empty state explains why it is empty, distinguishes no-results from never-created, and offers the most relevant next action rather than showing blank space or a bare message.
capabilities.rationale: The structural half is checkable — an empty state that renders dedicated content with an actionable affordance rather than nothing. Whether the offered action is the right one is judgment.

capabilities.title: Cards frame objects, not everything
capabilities.description: Containment is used for repeated records, focused tools, modals, and genuinely framed objects — while page structure is expressed through alignment, typography, whitespace, and separators instead of nested rounded rectangles.
capabilities.rationale: DESIGN.md already forbids wrapping whole page sections in floating cards, and the library ships Card as a near-default wrapper. Nesting depth and the ratio of containers to content are countable, which makes the worst cases detectable even if the judgment is not.

capabilities.title: Composition has rhythm, not just a grid
capabilities.description: Content-driven surfaces may use unequal dimensions, deliberate overlap, and variable rhythm where the content warrants it, without the layout becoming arbitrary.
capabilities.rationale: Declared because the current model assumes uniform components in uniform grids and cannot express anything else — which is a real ceiling on the editorial and content-first kits. Aspirational because there is no credible deterministic formulation of it yet, and pretending otherwise would produce a checker that punishes good work.

capabilities.title: The declared signature moment is realized
capabilities.description: The one interaction an asset declares as its signature — the moment a user would recognize without a logo — is actually present and behaves as described.
capabilities.rationale: Pairs with the per-asset `signatureMoment` field on the catalog descriptor. Its value is mostly in forcing the question at authoring time — an asset that cannot name its signature moment usually does not have one.

capabilities.title: Delight is allocated, not sprayed
capabilities.description: Emphatic feedback is reserved for genuinely significant completions; routine successes settle quietly, so the emphatic moments retain their meaning.
capabilities.rationale: Directly relevant to a system where agents complete work constantly. If every completed task celebrates, none of them mean anything, and the interface becomes exhausting to sit in front of.
